title: Canonical canary manifest language and simulator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a canonical, machine-validated canary manifest language (a small DSL/JSON schema) plus a standalone simulator that can execute manifests against historical or synthetic traffic. Goals: provide a single source of truth for traffic-splits, step schedules, guardrails, and auto-rollback conditions; make rollouts reproducible across hosted/dedicated/private deployments; enable deterministic dry-runs for PMs/SEs before real traffic; and provide developer-friendly validation errors and remediation suggestions.
acceptance_criteria: Define a compact manifest schema that models steps, traffic weights, cohort selectors, and guardrail expressions
Implement a CLI simulator that can ingest a manifest and replay historical telemetry (latency/errors) to produce per-step outcomes and a predicted rollback decision
Integrate manifest validation into the Console UI and the runtime admission controller with human-readable error messages
Add two end-to-end tests: one for a successful phased rollout, one that triggers auto-rollback based on a latency SLO breach
Document manifest grammar and example manifests for canary, A/B, and shadow workflows in the runbook repo
decisions: Use a JSON-schema-first approach for the canonical manifest so we can reuse existing validation libraries across services
Guardrail expressions will use a small expression language that maps to runtime metrics (p50/p95/error-rate) rather than embedding arbitrary JS
Simulator will be deterministic and seedable; it will support both sampled historical traces and synthetic distributions
Runtime will enforce manifests via the admission controller and fallback to the previous variant if the manifest fails validation or runtime compatibility checks
tasks: Spike: draft manifest schema and example manifests (completed)
Prototype: simulator CLI that replays synthetic latency distributions (in progress)
API: runtime admission validator for manifests and schema errors (blocked by RBAC mapping)

E2E: add rollout smoke tests to integration harness (depends on simulator)
Security: KMS/HSM review for manifests that reference encrypted parameters
